# Flyero

![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-5.9-3178C6?logo=typescript&logoColor=white)
![Node](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node-%3E%3D20-339933?logo=node.js&logoColor=white)
![MCP](https://img.shields.io/badge/MCP-server-6E56CF)

**One prompt in, one marketing flyer out, generated by a deterministic layout engine instead of an image model.**

Flyero turns a plain-language brief (plus an optional logo or product photo) into a 1080x1350 marketing flyer. The core idea is a strict separation of concerns: a language model decides *meaning* (the creative idea, the story, which components to use, the copy), while a deterministic TypeScript engine decides *geometry* (coordinates, type sizing, wrapping, collisions, contrast). LLMs are unreliable at spatial math and reliable at ideas, so the system only asks each side to do what it's good at. Every generated flyer is checked against six code-enforced quality gates before it can be marked "done"; a flyer that fails is returned honestly as `below_bar` rather than shipped anyway.

Flyero ships as a REST API with a thin MCP server on top of it, so it can be driven directly with `curl` or plugged into an MCP-capable client such as Claude or Cursor.

## Features

- **Prompt-to-flyer pipeline.** Ten internal stages (brief, sampling, ideation, composition, layout, render, critique, revision, gating, export) turn a text prompt into a finished PNG/SVG.
- **Diversity by construction.** Each job draws a random "designer" (a bundle of metaphor, layout topology, typography behavior, material, color logic, gesture and graphic language) from a curated combinatorial space, so repeated runs of the same prompt read like different human designers' work rather than reskins of one template.
- **Six quality gates, enforced in code.** One idea, cover test (is the product still recognizable with the logo and headline masked), restraint (4-7 justified elements), type participation, one signature gesture actually applied, and no hollow/invented copy. A flyer only ships if it clears all six.
- **A deterministic layout solver**, not a layout-generating LLM call. Grid placement, text wrapping, overlap and collision resolution, safe margins and WCAG-AA contrast checking are all pure TypeScript, so the same spec and seed always render identical pixels.
- **A hand-built component library.** 36 React/SVG components (headline blocks, photo clusters, before/after stacks, browser frames, score rings, composed figures, and more) that the composer/agent can only select from, never invent shapes outside of.
- **Multi-provider image sourcing.** One search call fans out across a dozen providers (Pexels, Unsplash, Pixabay, Openverse, Wikimedia, SVGRepo, Simple Icons, unDraw, Open Doodles, plus local shape and QR generators) for photos, icons, illustrations and scannable QR codes.
- **Asset preparation pipeline.** Uploaded logos and product photos go through sharp-based transforms (background removal, cropping, feathering, duotone, brand tinting) via named presets before they're placed in a design.
- **An agent-native composition path.** An MCP-connected agent can act as its own creative director: sample a designer lineage, choose components, write copy, and judge the render itself, with no server-side model key required.
- **Multiple output formats.** Portrait 4:5 (1080x1350), square 1:1 (1080x1080) and story 9:16 (1080x1920), with the layout solver re-running the topology recipe per format rather than stretching a fixed canvas.
- **PNG and editable SVG export**, with text kept as real `<text>` in the SVG rather than outlined paths. PDF export is planned but not yet implemented (the endpoint currently returns `501`).
- **A large automated test suite** covering the layout solver, gates, sampler distribution, image search and golden-snapshot rendering determinism.

## Tech stack

| Concern | Choice |
|---|---|
| Language / runtime | TypeScript, Node.js 20+ (run directly via `tsx`, no build step to plain JS) |
| API server | Fastify |
| Schema validation | Zod, shared between the API, the composer and the renderer |
| Rendering | React 18 `renderToStaticMarkup` to SVG, `@resvg/resvg-js` to rasterize PNG |
| LLM provider | Anthropic Claude (`@anthropic-ai/sdk`), abstracted behind `src/llm/` so it's swappable |
| MCP | `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`, both stdio and streamable HTTP transports |
| Job store | SQLite (`better-sqlite3`), with optional Postgres (`pg`) for persistent deployments |
| Object store | Local filesystem, configurable directory |
| Image processing | `sharp` for transforms, `qrcode` for scannable CTAs, `fontkit` for font metrics |
| Testing | Vitest (unit, golden-snapshot, and acceptance suites) |

## MCP tools

Running `npm run mcp` starts an MCP server exposing 17 tools over stdio (and streamable HTTP for hosted connectors). They split into two groups:

**Agent-native tools** (always available, no server-side API key required, the connected agent supplies the creative intelligence itself):

| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `read_design_guide` / `read_design_skill` | Load Flyero's design guide and judgement skills (composition, copywriting, critique) before composing |
| `request_designers` | Ask the Studio Sampler for candidate designer lineages for a campaign type |
| `search_images` / `import_image` | Search and pull in photos, icons, illustrations and QR codes across multiple providers |
| `search_motifs` | Search the recolorable vector motif library |
| `upload_asset` / `prepare_asset` | Upload a logo or product photo and transform it for a design slot |
| `get_composition_example` / `get_component_props` | Fetch schema shapes and per-component prop schemas |
| `compose_recipe` / `compose_flyer` | Compose a flyer by filling named slots, or by authoring a full elements/relationships graph |
| `revise_composition` | Edit an existing composition and re-render |
| `review_flyer` | Submit the agent's own judgement on the three gates that need a human/model eye |
| `export_composed_flyer` / `get_flyer` / `export_flyer` | Retrieve or export a finished flyer as PNG or SVG |

**Server-authored tools** (only registered when `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is set on the server, so the server runs the whole pipeline itself):

| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `create_flyer` | Hand a prompt to the server's own pipeline and get back a finished flyer |
| `revise_flyer` | Request a plain-language revision of a server-authored flyer |
| `create_flyer_batch` | Generate several independent versions of one brief for comparison |

## Getting started

Requires Node.js 20 or newer.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/DharambirAgrawal/flyero.git
cd flyero
npm install
npm run fonts     # one-time download of the open-license fonts used for rendering
cp .env.example .env
```

Fill in `.env`. Nothing is required to run the test suite or explore the pipeline offline; to run the full LLM-driven pipeline, set `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. To enable live stock photo search, set `PEXELS_API_KEY` and/or the other provider keys in `.env.example`.

## Usage

```bash
npm test               # full test suite (unit, golden-snapshot, acceptance); no API key needed
npm run sheet -- SEED 8   # render 8 sampled designers against the same brief, offline, to compare output diversity
npm start               # start the REST API (default port 8080)
npm run mcp              # start the MCP server over stdio
npm run smoke -- "Flyer for a weekend pottery workshop"   # live end-to-end run against real models
```

With the REST API running, a full generate/export loop looks like:

```bash
# create a job
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"prompt":"Flyer for a weekend pottery workshop, first class free."}' \
  localhost:8080/v1/flyers

# poll for status
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" localhost:8080/v1/flyers/fly_XXXX

# download the finished flyer
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" -o out.png \
  "localhost:8080/v1/flyers/fly_XXXX/export?format=png"
```

To use Flyero from an MCP client (Claude Desktop, Cursor, etc.), point it at `npm run mcp` (stdio) or the server's `/mcp` endpoint (streamable HTTP), and it will announce its own workflow through the server's MCP instructions.

## How it works

A generation job runs through ten stages, defined in `src/core/pipeline.ts`:

1. **Brief Builder** (LLM) turns the raw prompt and any uploaded assets into a structured brief: product, audience, objective, CTA, with every claim tagged as user-supplied, assumption, or placeholder.
2. **Studio Sampler** (seeded randomness, no LLM) draws several candidate "designer" lineages from one cryptographically random job seed, each forced into a different metaphor family. This is the mechanism that makes repeated runs of the same prompt diverge like independent human designers, rather than by history or memory of past output.
3. **Idea Engine** (LLM, constrained by the sampled lineage) produces a single-sentence visual idea and a four-beat story (problem, product acting, payoff, CTA).
4. **Composer** (LLM, validated against a Zod schema) turns the idea into a Design Spec: which components fill which roles, how they relate to each other (in front of, behind, annotates, points to), and the final copy. Components must come from the fixed Component Library; the composer cannot invent raw shapes.
5. **Layout Solver** (pure TypeScript, no LLM) converts that semantic spec into exact geometry: grid placement, coordinates, font sizing, text wrapping, overlap and collision resolution, safe margins, and contrast-aware color assignment. Each of the ~14 composition topologies ships as a parameterized recipe that the solver fits content into, rather than running general constraint optimization.
6. **Renderer** renders the spec to SVG via React's `renderToStaticMarkup`, then rasterizes to PNG with `resvg`. Given the same spec and seed, output is byte-identical, which the golden-snapshot tests enforce.
7. **Critic** runs a fast rule-based pass first (overflow, contrast, margins, banned-pattern detection) and, if that passes, a multimodal vision pass on the rendered PNG that judges what code can't: whether the idea reads, whether anything collides, whether the hierarchy holds up.
8. **Reviser** applies the critic's fixes as targeted spec edits (never a full regeneration) and loops back to layout, capped at a configurable number of revision rounds.
9. **Gatekeeper** runs the six quality gates and a set of mechanical checks (overflow, WCAG-AA contrast against the actual rendered background, safe margins, CTA presence, banned-pattern clearance, ink coverage, collision detection) on every candidate. Among candidates that pass, a comparative selection step picks the most "authored" result rather than just the highest score; if nothing passes, the pipeline can retry once with a fresh set of lineages before honestly returning `below_bar`.
10. **Exporter** produces the PNG for delivery, an editable SVG (with real, named text nodes), and the spec JSON.

Three or more lineages run stages 3 through 8 in parallel per job, all pulling from one shared vision-call budget so cost per flyer stays bounded regardless of how many candidates need extra revision passes.

There are two ways a flyer actually gets composed: the server-authored path (`POST /v1/flyers`), where Flyero's own pipeline calls Claude at every LLM-shaped stage, and the agent-native path (`POST /v1/flyers/compose`), where a connected MCP agent does the creative thinking itself and Flyero only supplies geometry, typography, and the gates. Both converge on the same layout, render, and gate pipeline.

## Documentation

Detailed design and engineering docs live in [`docs/`](docs/), including [`ARCHITECTURE.md`](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) (pipeline design), [`FLYERO-OVERVIEW.md`](docs/FLYERO-OVERVIEW.md) (a working reference written against the actual code), [`API.md`](docs/API.md) (the full REST and MCP surface), [`SCHEMAS.md`](docs/SCHEMAS.md) (data contracts), and [`ROADMAP.md`](docs/ROADMAP.md) (build order and current milestone status).

## Status

Under active development. The end-to-end pipeline, component library, Studio Sampler, layout solver, REST API and MCP server are built and tested. The next milestone on the roadmap is a formal diversity evaluation: verifying that ten independent runs of the same prompt are reliably distinguishable as different designers' work, which is the core premise the product is built around.
